source.title: On Feature Diversity in Energy-based Models
source.authors: Firas Laakom; Jenni Raitoharju; Alexandros Iosifidis; M. Gabbouj

record.file_problem: Full paper text, including supplementary material, is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper tests whether feature-diversity regularization changes generalization-related outcomes in energy-based models, using different models, tasks, and measures than the claim versions specify.
record.gate_note: Reports theoretical bounds and experimental results for feature-diversity regularization. Rows below cover reported numeric task results. The paper does not test random-label memorization, width past interpolation, convolutional versus fully connected generalization, optimizer or batch-size comparisons, dropout, magnitude-aware sharpness, or removal of memorized examples.
record.test_reason: The study derives feature-diversity bounds and evaluates its own diversity regularizer for energy-based models. Neither its theory nor its experiments test V1–V8. Using Adam, fully connected networks, and convolutional networks in separate experiments supplies none of the comparisons those versions require.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially accurate. The authors conclude that feature redundancy reduction improves their theoretical generalization bounds and that preliminary experiments motivate further evaluation. Their assertion of consistent regression improvement conflicts with two printed Table 1 entries. Tighter bounds should be distinguished from demonstrated reductions in realized generalization gaps.
record.recipe_differences: The study introduces feature-diversity regularization for energy-based models and tests it on regression, continual learning, and MNIST generation; it does not reproduce the cited claim methods.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported outcomes vary with dataset, noise parameter σ1, regularizer coefficient β, and continual-learning setting (boundary-aware or boundary-agnostic).

fits_no_version.finding: Theorems 1–4 give energy generalization-gap upper bounds that decrease with feature diversity when the other bound quantities are held fixed. Section 2.4 notes dependence on feature norms.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Greater feature diversity can tighten the derived EBM generalization bounds under their assumptions; this does not establish lower realized test error.

fits_no_version.finding: Diversity regularization lowers printed regression KL or NLL in most settings. Two KL entries worsen: 0.3450 versus 0.0420 and 0.0377 versus 0.0374.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Feature-diversity regularization improves most reported EBM regression metrics, with dependence on coefficient and noise setting.

fits_no_version.finding: All regularized Table 2 mean accuracies exceed their corresponding EBM baselines; the paper reports SEMs but no significance tests.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Feature-diversity regularization yields higher mean class-incremental accuracy in the tested CIFAR settings.

fits_no_version.finding: All regularized MNIST-generation mean FID and NLL values are slightly lower than baseline; uncertainty is reported over three runs.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Feature-diversity regularization yields modest improvements in reported mean MNIST-generation metrics.

record.problems: The authors describe the experimental results as preliminary; the main experiments are on two 1-D regression datasets and continual learning, and the MNIST generation results are supplementary. The paper notes that its diversity measure is not scale invariant. Some reported numeric task metrics are not directly generalization gaps or held-out error comparisons.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting versus natural-label held-out accuracy under the same architecture and recipe.
Width beyond zero training error and its effect on test error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image-classification performance and the role of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under comparable tuning.
Batch-size comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that recover performance.
Dropout effects, including training-set size, dropout strength, and interactions with augmentation and weight decay.
Magnitude-aware perturbation sharpness, its correlation with generalization gaps, and comparisons with other measures.
Removing highly memorized examples versus removing random examples and retraining.

record.verdict_notes: T6 applies relative to V1–V8. The paper cites original sources [46] and [47] concerning loose generalization bounds, without testing their specific claims. All existing version links remain none; cannot_determine indicates that these rows cannot establish any listed version, rather than that their task metrics are unreadable. Table 1 values are means over 20 seeds.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and generalization on natural labels.
Width sweep beyond the interpolation threshold and test error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image-classification generalization.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer held-out performance.
Large versus small batch generalization gap under epoch budgets.
Magnitude-aware sharpness as a measure tracking the training-test gap.
Removing memorized examples and measuring test accuracy.
